humanScope: 2024-09-24 is the main bull/bear split. Primary evaluation remains post-split net realized payoff, liquidity and excess returns; bear profitability is not required. No numerical success threshold has been confirmed by the human.
modelDecisions: Gross cash and actual additional shares are distinct from virtual ex-reference terms. Source dates and missing fields are explicit.
Historical OHLC is compared in the as-of close's units using only already-effective, dated events. Raw bars/amount/volume stay unchanged; the output is price continuity, not portfolio total return.
Bonus shares increase lots and preserve total entry cost. Risk entry/peak and stale marks are converted once; the volatility ratchet ratio stays invariant.

Floor/ceil account-level fractional share allocations are named sensitivities. Largest-remainder lot allocation is a deterministic research convention, not evidence of actual CSDC shareholder allocation.

A required fixed tax-reserve rate is an explicit scenario. Gross receivable, provisional tax liability, paid reserved cash and spendable cash are separate. This is not an investor-specific duration/FIFO tax assessment.
Date-only dividends are spendable at the first processed opening strictly after scheduled pay-date. This conservative model does not assert a broker credit timestamp.
Receivables and dividend income remain bound to the original entry episode even if the symbol is later reentered.
Ex-day pending buys retain their frozen T-close quantity and acquire no prior-record entitlement. Saved exits are retained; locked grants can require later partial fills.

A missing ex-bar keeps valuation stale and blocks fills requiring the missing prior session. Price-continuity comparison converts the old observation's units without inventing a missing tradable quote.
Unexplained raw/reference discontinuities remain quarantined. Day rollback restores cash, lot rights, dividend claims, risk ratchets, opportunities and fees.

permissionBoundary: Local isolated research only; no protected user JSON changes, actual orders, commit, push, packaging or publication.
